objective: KI-45: do the explicit session trace buffers (netwatch.BUFFERS: 256 KB, 64 to 512 buffers, at most 128 MB) keep the M1 network monitor from losing events, where logman's defaults lost 1203 in EXP-048 session 1, and do all the EXP-046 coverage cases still hold with them?
hypothesis: Run elevated, the new case flood_with_session_buffers (200000 loopback UDP datagrams, the flood that lost events with the tiny buffers in EXP-046) is a MATCH: covered, 0 events lost, the flood attributed to the stand-in, and the stand-in's status records that all 200000 sends completed (Codex pass 9). Review #39 (FB-39-03), added at the owner's request and approved in chat on 2026-10-28: a ninth case, mixed_load_with_session_buffers, is a MATCH too. One stand-in does every kind of traffic, one after the other (IPv6 loopback TCP and UDP, 50 brief loopback TCP connections, the 200000 flood, a DNS lookup, a public UDP send, a child's public UDP send), while for its whole life unrelated stand-ins, not targets, each send 400000 loopback datagrams, a finished one replaced within 50 ms. It must be covered with 0 events lost, every kind attributed to the target or its child (the flood too), and every stand-in's record complete. A send refused through the stand-in's status is NOT_APPLICABLE; a stand-in that stops early (for example a refused flood send) is a MISMATCH (Codex pass 13). The seven EXP-046 cases give the same verdicts as in EXP-046. The dry run (dryrun.py, EXP-045's cases) still gives 11/11 with the session buffers. This is fixed before the runs. It measures a stand-in's burst, not the game: a real session's background load can differ, which is why the session record now keeps events_total and buffers.
environment: Windows 11 Pro x64, Python 3.15, logman and tracerpt from Windows; the stand-in is tools/m1/standin.py, not the game; dev machine
game_exe_sha256: N/A (the experiment never touches the game, its files or its saves)
procedure: On the amended code, python -I tools/m1/coverage.py and python -I tools/m1/dryrun.py, each once without elevation (Claude Code; every case must be not_covered or INCONCLUSIVE) and once from an elevated PowerShell (the owner). coverage.py writes evidence/logs/m1-coverage-<time>-<elevated|not-elevated>/result.json, now labelled EXP-050 and with the buffers used. No threshold is tuned after a run: if the flood case is a MISMATCH, the buffer sizes are a new decision, recorded before another run.
expected_result: No MISMATCH in either coverage run (flood_with_session_buffers and mixed_load_with_session_buffers a MATCH elevated); dryrun 11/11 elevated.
observed_result: Without elevation (Claude Code, clean commit 4c5ef08): coverage.py 9/9 not_covered, as expected, NO MISMATCH (evidence/logs/m1-coverage-2026-10-28-151626-not-elevated); the mixed-load case ran end to end, its target's actions all sent and one background stand-in complete. dryrun.py: all cases match (evidence/logs/m1-dryrun-2026-10-28-151640-not-elevated). The elevated runs, the ones that measure the buffers, are the owner's and have not run.
follow_up: With EXP-050 passed and reviewed, the owner decides on the amended section 8 (EXP-051).
